silhouette.reason: Reads as a grey wolf from every view: long muzzle, pricked ears, deep chest, tucked belly, long straight legs and a hanging brush tail; the SIDE view in sheet.png gives the standing-wolf outline at once.
fixes: give the neck ruff a broken, tufted outline (a short shell or card pass) so the head does not join the shoulders in one smooth curve

proportions.reason: 1.2 × 0.3 × 0.9 m on the grid sits inside the sourced adult range; leg length, chest depth and head size look right beside photos. The tail hangs to the hocks, at the long end of the range.
fixes: shorten the tail a few centimetres in a Blender step so it ends above the hock, as on most reference photos

materials.reason: The image-to-3D texture reads as a grizzled grey coat with a pale chest and legs, and the face markings hold. Lighting is baked into the albedo (bright back, saturated orange flank and ear patches) and the fur has one uniform roughness.
fixes: de-light the albedo before import (a bake step that divides out the baked sun and AO)
pull the orange patches on the flank, ears and tail toward the coat's tawny grey

detail.reason: Fur breakup, eyes, nose and toes come from the texture and hold at third-person distance. Geometry is smooth: no fur clumps on the outline, and the flank shows rib-like ridges in SIDE that read as a starved animal rather than a coat.
fixes: smooth the ridges on the flank in a Blender sculpt step
a strand or shell pass on the ruff, back and tail so the outline breaks into fur clumps

wear.reason: A clean animal: the darker back gives a little story, but there is no mud on the paws or lower legs, no wet or matted fur, no scars.
fixes: mud on the paws and lower legs (grime with the ground mask over the textured part)
a seeded scar on the muzzle or a nicked ear

lod.reason: FAR LOD2 keeps the outline, the pale chest and the dark back; at the sheet's far distance it is hard to tell from LOD0.
fixes: lower the LOD2 triangle count: the far view does not need its current budget for a 1.2 m animal

technical.reason: QA PASS and one draw per LOD, with idle, look and walk clips, but only with a declared deform tolerance: the skin webs between the tail root and the thighs at the hip's extremes (stretch up to ×5.7 against a limit of ×4, defect D253, still open).
fixes: close D253: a per-bone reach or blend at the tail root in the `isolate` Blender step, or a regenerated mesh from a concept with one raised tail, then remove `limitTolerances`
